label: Card Provider Info
title: Card Provider Info
summary: Use a Card Provider Info to introduce who provides a product, with their logo and a few short facts in two columns.
corePrinciple: Who provides it, and why to trust them.

anatomy.title: A provider and its facts
anatomy.description: A rounded card puts the provider’s logo and name on top, then lays its children out two to a row. The facts are StatItem components: a small label over a large value.

A StatItem child: a 12 px label over a 26 px value.
Children sit two to a row, 8 px apart, each half the width.

configuration.title: Brand and avatar size
configuration.description: AppearanceBrand sets the card’s fill: Primary cream by default, Secondary lilac, and Neutral or Tertiary white with a light border. The label and the facts stay the same colour. The logo is Figma’s 29 px; Avatar Size L makes it 42 px, and showAvatar={false} hides it.
blocks: The default: a cream card, as in Figma.
White with a light border; Tertiary looks the same.

states.title: Facts only, by default
states.description: The card shows facts and does nothing when tapped. onPress makes the whole card one button, named by accessibilityLabel or label; it doesn’t change its look when pressed, and disabled only stops presses. Don’t put buttons among the facts of a pressable card.
blocks: The whole card is one button and looks the same.

examples.title: Pressable
examples.description: The whole card is one button and looks the same.

sizing.title: Your screen sets the width
sizing.description: The card fills its host’s width; Figma draws it at 342 px. It has 20 px padding and 20 px between the header and the facts, and each fact takes half the width with 8 px between them. Height follows the content: 199 px with four facts and the 29 px logo.

content.title: Short facts with their figures
content.description: Put the provider’s name in label. Give each fact a short noun phrase for its label and the figure for its value: values are large and heavy, so keep them to a few characters. Two to six facts, in pairs, read best.
blocks: The third fact sits alone and leaves a gap beside it.

inContext.title: The provider on the Buy Gold screen
inContext.description: The screen supplies the provider’s logo, name, and facts. The card only shows them; the Buy button below is the screen’s own action.

doDont.title: Short facts from a known provider
doDont.description: Each pair shows a card people trust at a glance next to one that crowds its facts or shows the wrong picture.

sources.title: Use the public Card Provider Info contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at c7d3348 (19 October) and taken from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card/Provider Info is one 342 × 185 component with no properties of its own; its Product Label can hide the avatar, and in code showAvatar does the same. The header comes from label and imageSource: without imageSource it shows the name alone, so this page passes the Jio Gold logo from the Figma component. The logo is Figma’s 29 px (Avatar Size S) by default. Fact rows are 50 px in code and 44 in Figma. The published Storybook still shows the older build, with a placeholder portrait, and the older generated page.
